questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from flat mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a better view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are used on many motorcycles. They show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they can make other vehicles look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What is a difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield stops your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: How should you position your body on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
Stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Good riding posture means using your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Sit so your elbows are slightly bent when you grip the handlebars.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcyclist most visible to other drivers?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When following a car, the center lane position is usually best. It puts your motorcycle in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if needed.

questions.question: What is the best position within a lane to ride in?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Good riders change their position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Keep going and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When being passed, which part of the lane should a motorcyclist be in?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation.

questions.question: What usually causes a "wobble" or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars?

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
The front wheel is not tightened properly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: A wobble is shaking of the front wheel and handlebars. Most wobbles result from improper weight loading, unsuitable accessories, or wrong tire pressure.

questions.question: Where do oil drippings and debris usually collect in a lane?

options.text: The left portion
The middle portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You may go over the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may ignore no-passing zone markings if you started the pass in a legal zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed at or below the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard in the road, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
Change your speed as needed.
Alert others by using your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you are doing. Use your horn, lights, and signals to show them where you are. Slow down or speed up to match the situation. Move to a different part of the lane or change direction if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must stop completely.
You can go through carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop completely.
questions.explanation: A red arrow on a traffic signal means the same as a red light. You must stop completely. Wait for a signal that lets you turn the way you want to go.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
Go ahead slowly.
Turn around and find another way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: Which one does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How much alcohol they drank
How fast they drank it
How often they usually drink

questions.correctAnswerText: How often they usually drink
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how fast it is consumed. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually stay in control.
You will likely lose control.
You must release the rear brake to get control back.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually stay in control.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can be used by someone with:

options.text: Only during daytime hours.
No driver license.
Any type of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any type of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane:

options.text: Must always be avoided.
Is safe to ride on except when it rains.
Should only be used if another vehicle is in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to ride on except when it rains.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually gives good grip for riding, unless it is wet from rain. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so riders can ride on either side of it and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle depends on:

options.text: Staying on the left side next to the center line.
Staying on the right side next to the curb.
Road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best position changes depending on the situation. Choose where you can see the best and have the most space around you. Move your position as traffic and road conditions change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This is a traffic law sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers what they cannot do in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When turning safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean your body in the direction you are turning.
Slow down while in the turn.
Turn using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean your body in the direction you are turning.
questions.explanation: Always lean your body in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.
